name: Perilous Valley

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The Perilous Valley is a Breton site in the legendary forest of Brocéliande, in Brittany. Morgan, King Arthur's half sister and the lover of the faithless Guyomard, set a curse on the valley. The curse made any man who had betrayed a woman get lost in the valley, wander as if pixy-led, and never find the way out. To a faithless knight such as Guyomard, the green valley seemed full of monsters, all of his own imagining. In the middle lay a lake called Fairy's Mirror. Nightmares rose from it like mist. Every knight who entered the valley believed he was alone. Gawain, a knight of King Arthur's court, was caught in the trap. Lancelot went to save him. Because Lancelot never betrayed Guinevere, he broke the enchantment and freed the captives.
